chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Art Tatum in Chicago and Los Angeles
summary: Tatum cut down every piano player, and Young later lived in the same Los Angeles apartment building as Tatum.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Tatum was playing in Chicago then wasn't he?
Yes, he was. Very much so. Yeah. Watch out when he came around, boy. He was -- he would really put all the piano players out of business.
Did he and Earl every play the same place, the same time. I mean like late after hours.
Not that I can recall but I imagine they

did because they both were very proud guys, you know. They both could play, you know. So, I imagine they did. I know Tatum -- anywhere a piano player was, he'd go, you know. He was like a lion, man, a roaring lion. This was his cup of tea, you know. He would do it all -- I don't care where a piano player was, he would go. He'd find him, you know. And he never stopped playing.

I lived in a -- in later years I lived in an apartment building out in Los Angeles where Tatum lived. And he had a piano up there. And he'd play all day. When he got up -- I could tell you when he got up. He'd -- before he -- he'd jam all night after he worked, and he'd go to bed. But when he got up, he would -- I could tell when he got up. He would start playing.
